rounds.text: Dollar Industries Ltd is significantly under-appreciated by the market, trading at a modest P/E of 13.7x and an EV/EBITDA of just 7.5x, which represent massive discounts to sector benchmarks of 47.88x and 34.45x respectively [E1, E6, E11]. Profit growth has been exceptionally strong recently, with trailing twelve-month profit growth hitting 23% and 3-year compounded profit growth reaching 22% [E20, E21]. This robust earnings power is backed by stellar cash generation, highlighted by an operating cash flow of Rs 137 Cr, a free cash flow of Rs 94 Cr, and a healthy cash conversion ratio of 1.29x in Mar 2026 [E33, E34, E35]. Balance sheet strength further underpins the value case, as borrowings decreased to Rs 264 Cr and the debt-to-equity ratio sits at a conservative 0.28x [E37, E38], while operating margins have structurally expanded by 4 percentage points over three years to 11% [E29]. Foreign institutional interest is also building, with foreign holdings increasing to 2.55% from 0.33% [E41]. Conceded: the stock sits near its 52-week lows, lags behind the broader market with a relative-strength rating of 0, and has experienced negative share price growth over the past 1, 3, and 5 years [E5, E22, E23, E24, E50].

Conceded: the company trades at a P/E of 13.7x and an EV/EBITDA of 7.5x [E1, E11], but these low multiples reflect persistent structural decay in market confidence and severe historical underperformance [E22, E23, E24]. The bull points to recent 23% trailing profit growth [E21], but glosses over a lackluster 5-year compounded profit growth of just 4% and a low 3-year median return on equity of 11% [E19, E27]. Furthermore, the official rules-based screen scores the business at a weak 44 out of 100 with low confidence, designating it merely neutral [E60]. While operating cash flow reached Rs 137 Cr in Mar 2026 [E34], the yearly operating-margin trend reads inconsistent over the last two years and quarterly margins contracted by 1 percentage point year-over-year [E30, E31]. The bull highlights foreign institutional buying [E41], but ignores the broader institutional outflow resulting in a negative money flow signal and a relative-strength rating of 0 against the Nifty 500 [E43, E50]. Finally, the stock trades below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages at just 19% to 20% of its 52-week range, confirming that downward momentum far outweighs any cheap multiple argument [E5, E47, E49].
